I give up on this one. The file is unchanged, and it still contains the `sorry`.

**What I could establish:**

- **Membership of 1/4 is easy.** Take `g n = n^2`. Then `g(g n)^(1/4) = ((n^2)^2)^(1/4) = n`, and `g(n+1) - g n = 2n + 1 ≥ n`. So the set contains `1/4`, and this half could be formalized without much trouble.
- **The upper bound is the hard part.** I need: any `r` admitting such a `g` satisfies `r ≤ 1/4`. Heuristically, if `g(n) ≈ n^a` then `g(g(n))^r ≈ n^(a²r)` must be at most `g(n+1) - g(n) ≈ n^(a-1)`, which forces `a²r ≤ a-1`. That has no solution `a` when `r > 1/4`. But the heuristic only covers polynomial growth. I did not find a rigorous argument for arbitrary `g`, including super-polynomially growing ones. The monotonicity facts I derived (`g(n) ≥ n`, `g(m) - g(n) ≥ (m-n)·g(g(n))^r`, `g(g(n))^r ≤ g(n+1) - g(n)`) were not enough to reach a contradiction.

I did not write a partial proof with `sorry`, since the task requires a complete proof with no `sorry`.

I give up.
